answer.answer:
**Summary**

Three firms recur across more than one joint development in the retrieved records: Firm_060, which appears in three of them, and Firm_061 and Firm_082, each in two. Firm_060 is the most connected, partnering with different groups on three separate robots, two of which work in steel, and one of which is the census record behind a deployed process. All other firms in front of me appear in a single partnership each, including a seven-firm consortium led with Firm_177. These are the joint-development records that retrieval returned rather than the full register, so the counts are floors, not totals, and the underlying graph encodes manufacturer and developer roles rather than a named co-development relation.

**Detailed answer**

**Firms appearing in more than one partnership**

Firm_060 appears in three census records:
- census_RXM6-4, jointly developed by Firm_168, Firm_060, Firm_008, Firm_009 and Firm_064 [1]. In the edge data Firm_168, Firm_060 and Firm_008 hold the manufacturer role while Firm_009 and Firm_064 are distributors, and this record is the census record of process RP14, so it is the one entry here tied to a deployed process record.
- census_RXM6-7, jointly developed by Firm_060, Firm_061 and Firm_079 [2], a steel-working machine.
- census_RXM6-6, jointly developed by Firm_060 and Firm_061 [3], also steel.

Firm_061 appears in two, census_RXM6-7 and census_RXM6-6, in both cases alongside Firm_060, which is the tightest repeated pairing in this set.

Firm_082 appears in two, with a different partner each time: census_RXM8-3 with Firm_072 [4] and census_RXM8-1 with Firm_003 [5].

**Firms appearing once here**

census_RXM23-5 was jointly developed by Firm_177, Firm_002, Firm_018, Firm_068, Firm_094, Firm_134 and Firm_209 [6], the largest consortium in this material at seven manufacturers. census_RXH8-2 was jointly developed by Firm_097 and Firm_098 [7], working in timber. census_RXH5-4 was jointly developed by Firm_027, Firm_028 and Firm_033 [8], recorded under a developedBy relation rather than hasManufacturer.

**What the evidence does and does not establish**

The recurrence counts above are exact for the records in front of me, but nothing licenses treating them as totals: this is a retrieved selection of census records, so a firm shown here once may hold further partnerships elsewhere in the register, and firms absent here are not absent from the record.

None of these census records is linked in the context to any enabler, so I cannot say which capabilities these co-developments activate. It is worth noting separately that the dependency evidence retrieved alongside them speaks to organisational coupling in general terms rather than to these firms: integrated design and digital fabrication processes are argued to have tighter organisational coupling as a precondition, with technically interdependent systems pushing work into a single firm, backed by peer-reviewed evidence [1], and interdisciplinary team integration is given as an enabler of the same, also peer-reviewed [1]. That enabler, integrated design and digital fabrication, is activated in 19 of the 50 coded cases. Whether the multi-firm arrangements above are instances of that pattern or a counterweight to it is not something the context settles.
